what.text: This page follows refugees from Sudan living in Libya, which UNHCR's data lists as the Libyan Arab Jamahiriya.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 551727 Sudanese refugees there, 19.6% of all Sudanese refugees.
Chad and South Sudan host more.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Sudan from 1990 to 2018 and from 2020 to 2025, at war level from 2023.
From 2020 to 2025 the opposing groups include the RSF, the SLM/A, the SPLM/A-North and the SFA.

when.text: UNHCR's figure rose from 199388 at the end of 2024 to 551727 at the end of 2025.
Big changes came between 2023 and 2024 and again between 2024 and 2025, and 2025 is the main year of displacement in the data.
Returns from Libya to Sudan were highest in 2011 in UNHCR's returns data.

how.text: These are year-end totals of refugees in Libya only, and UNHCR adds notes to some of them.
Gender and age are known for only part of this group.
The sources don't say which routes people took or where in Libya they live.
